item.title: Scientists tagged 14,000 endangered moths with paint and glue; none turned up, and that may be good news
item.description: In a groundbreaking study, researchers have tagged over 14,000 Bogong moths in the Snowy Mountains of Australia. However, after extensive tracking efforts, none have been recaptured, suggesting potential populations larger than previously assumed. Alternatively, these moths might be utilizing undiscovered migration routes. The ongoing project remains crucial for understanding the ecology of these endangered insects. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Alleged killers of Australian, US surfers go on trial in Mexico
item.description: Three men on trial for killing Jake and Callum Robinson and Jack Carter Rhoad in Baja California in 2024 The alleged killers of two Australian surfers and an American at a Mexican surfing hotspot in 2024 have gone on trial in the border resort where the three were murdered. The Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, aged 30 and 33, respectively, and their 30-year-old American friend Jack Carter Rhoad were shot dead after being robbed in Mexico’s violence-hit Baja California . item.title: An Australian woman learned she was pregnant and could give birth ‘any day’ within 24 hours
item.description: An Australian mother was shocked to find out she was pregnant just days before giving birth to a very premature baby. Her daughter, Makerita Tanuvasa, entered the world at just 21 weeks and three days, weighing only 351 grams. Remarkably, she became Australia’s most premature surviving infant. After more than four months in intensive care, receiving specialized treatment, she finally returned home, marking a miraculous recovery. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: North Korea and Russia open their first road bridge, a symbol of expanding ties
item.description: Connection across Tumen River is further sign of closer ties between the two countries since start of war in Ukraine Russia and North Korea have opened the first road bridge across their shared border , in the latest sign of the rapidly deepening ties between the two countries since the start of the war in Ukraine. The one-kilometre bridge spans the Tumen River between Khasan in Russia’s far east and Tumangang in North Korea, along a remote and sparsely populated stretch of the countries’ shared border just a few miles from the coast. Continue reading... Publicado también por: South China Morning Post, ABC News Australia, The Guardian - World. Fuente: The Jerusalem Post - International.
